build.prompt_version: Trump Diary — Weekly Thread Package Prompt v1

week.headline: The twenty-fifth week of Trump’s second term did not hinge on a single shock.

What distinguished this period was not novelty but convergence: the presidency, the courts, and the security apparatus moved together to widen executive freedom, hollow out neutral capacity, and raise the cost of dissent. thread_states.canonical_name: Executive overreach through emergency claims, unilateral action, and weakened checks

evidence_items.title: Courts and presidency move together to widen executive freedom
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The week summary explicitly frames the period as one in which institutional checks weakened and executive discretion widened, making constitutional overreach a central explanatory frame rather than a side effect.

evidence_items.title: Coordinated tightening across law and state power
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The digest-level framing emphasizes convergence among legal and state institutions, supporting this thread as one of the main drivers of the week.

evidence_items.title: Multiple domains treated as parts of one governing pattern
evidence_items.why_it_matters: Allocator framing suggests the week is organized around executive latitude expanding across issue areas, which is characteristic of this thread.

thread_states.summary: Week 25 is best understood as a consolidation week for executive maximalism: not a single emergency spectacle, but a broad widening of presidential freedom as other institutions either aligned with or failed to restrain it.
continuity_notes: This reads as an extension of the prior week rather than a fresh constitutional rupture.
The week should stress normalization of expanded executive discretion, not only isolated abuses.
Carry forward the sense that weakened checks now operate as governing structure, not temporary exception.

evidence_items.title: Neutral capacity weakened across agencies
evidence_items.why_it_matters: The week is described as hollowing out neutral state capacity, making this thread central to how the machinery of power is functioning.

evidence_items.title: Agency-level control as a cross-cutting development
evidence_items.why_it_matters: Allocator evidence likely groups disparate policy actions under bureaucratic subordination, reinforcing this as a lead thread for rewrite structure.

thread_states.summary: Administrative capture is one of the main mechanisms of the week: agencies are not merely implementing policy but being stripped of neutrality and repurposed as instruments of political control.
continuity_notes: Continue prior emphasis on state control moving from staffing and purges into operational mission rewrites.
Public health and other expert institutions should be treated as examples of capture, not separate technocratic stories.
This thread pairs closely with executive overreach but should remain distinct as the machinery layer.

evidence_items.title: Immigration developments linked to domestic control

Connect information control to public-health and education examples if they appear in the rewrite.
Keep this thread as an integrating support, not the sole narrative driver.

week_summary_notes: Week 25 is defined less by novelty than by convergence: several authoritarian threads move together at once.
The strongest narrative frame is institutional tightening across executive power, bureaucracy, immigration, and security-state capacity.
Law and information control matter chiefly as parts of the same system, not as isolated scandals.
The rewrite should avoid overloading the chapter with every possible thread and instead show how multiple mechanisms reinforced one another.
Dissent suppression is present as an effect of the week’s convergence and can be treated as a reactivated supporting thread rather than the sole lead.

rewrite_guidance.opening_focus: Open on the week as a coordinated tightening rather than a single headline event: executive freedom widened while bureaucracy, border policy, and coercive state power increasingly worked in concert.
rewrite_guidance.closing_focus: Close on the normalization of convergence itself—the fact that law, administration, immigration, and security mechanisms were no longer acting episodically but as a joined system that raised the cost of dissent and narrowed neutral civic space.
continuity_emphasis_notes: Emphasize continuation and consolidation more than rupture.
Show how immigration and administrative capture function as operational machinery for executive overreach.
Use security-state and legal-pressure examples to illustrate the cost imposed on dissent and opposition.
Treat schools, churches, and public-health institutions as evidence that the project reached deeply into social and knowledge institutions.
Avoid introducing unrelated threads that would dilute the chapter’s central convergence frame.
